newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran cleric says Tehran may retaliate against U.S..
newsitem.headline: Iran cleric says Tehran may retaliate against U.S..

text.p: A senior Iranian cleric denounced on Friday U.S. media attempts to link Iran to an attack on a U.S. military complex in Saudi Arabia and said his country would retaliate against any possible punitive U.S. strike.

The Unites States has not yet concluded who was responsible for the June bombing but Iranian officials have said recently that Washington is preparing to attack Iran for the incident at the Dhahran base in which 19 U.S. airmen were killed.

"They (U.S.) do not let go," Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati, a member of the powerful Guardian Council, said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast live on state-run Tehran radio and monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) radio.

"Now there has been an incident in Dhahran, there has been an explosion and several Americans have been killed. They are accusing Shi'ism and Iran despite the fact they do not have any evidence, not even a shred of evidence to indicate that Iran has had a part in it in any way," he added.

"Then there are the threats; they say they might resort to action some day and take revenge. It is mostly because of the consumption of alcoholic drinks; there is no doubt that alcohol has to a certain degree numbed their powers of judgment," Jannati added.

"However, we hope they will not resort to crazy measures," he added. "But at any rate, we are ready to confront any act of sedition and corruption. And we shall not shy away from any confrontation and retaliation."
